# Quantum Timestamped Entanglement

> Timestamped single-click links retain relative-phase coherence across arrivals. A local three-herald receiver converts that coherence into usable Bell pairs without observing the optical phase.

## Read the result

- [Overview and principal results](README.md)
- [Source and timing model](science/model.md): raw link states, public timestamps, hidden source labels, finite and stream output contracts.
- [Three-herald receiver](science/receiver.md): local excitation counting, qutrit filtering, Bell fidelity and a matched two-input upper bound.
- [Robustness and wall time](science/robustness.md): dephasing, both false-click products, a flagged instrument error budget, finite and windowed examples.
- [Poisson-stream proof](science/stream.md): arbitrary timestamp-aware LOCC converse, contiguous conditional mutual information and the clean next-order gain.

## Study and reproduce

- [Wilde bridge](learning/WILDE_BRIDGE.md): selected 2017 second edition and one worked triple.
- [Thirty milestones](learning/MILESTONES.md): background and connected project route.
- [Verification](verification/README.md): run `python3 verification/check.py` with NumPy.
- [Related work](references/RELATED_WORK.md) and [BibTeX bibliography](references/references.bib).

## Scope

The finite upper bound permits arbitrary processing of one timestamp-selected raw dyad from the supplied triple. In the robustness comparison the dyad receiver gets ideal storage and may decode early. The finite noisy receiver meets a Bell fidelity target averaged over accepted outputs. The ideal stream rate counts distilled ebits per elapsed time, with the long observation limit before the sparse limit. The q² leading factor uses one false-click product state; the clean second coefficient assumes all heralds genuine. The three-cell memory count is for raw links at each endpoint. Outer hashing requires additional block storage.
